summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught at Rumtek Monastery (1959, 1967) and served as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Bokar Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.
He studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga. His students included Chatral Sangye Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Önpo Tenzin Norbu, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo, among others. He taught at Shri Singha Shedra (1902) and became Dzongsar Monastery's first khenpo in 1918.
He studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

In Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Lama Zolpa Trinlé. He served as principal teacher at Rumtek Monastery's shedra and as spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery in 1992.
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (~1984–2004) and Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel.

In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Dudjom Rinpoche, Kangyur Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and others. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1960–1970), Kyoto University (1960–1970), and the University of Virginia (~1980).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, among others. He held teaching posts at Lhasa Mentsikhang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Active in Tibetology, he studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen, and taught students including Yeshi Dhonden.
Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

In Buddhist studies, he earned his MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and also studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, John Kieschnick, Barend J. ter Haar, and Seishi Karashima (2013).

In philosophy, he studied at First Higher School, University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), and University of Freiburg (1920). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918, 1923, 1926, 1930–1945), Hokkaido University (1947, 1950–1951), and Chuo University (1951–1958).
In Tibetology and religious studies, she earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
In religious studies and Indology, she held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

In Indology and history/archaeology, she studied at Haverford College and Brown University (PhD 1995 under David Pingree). She held posts at Brown (1989), MIT (2000–2004), Utrecht (2004–2005), and Union College (2007, 2012, 2019).

Specializing in religious studies, she completed her dissertation at Harvard University. She was an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and Assistant Professor in the Comparative and Historical Study of Religion at Harvard (~1993).

In Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he studied at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1989), Eastern Institute (attested 1996, 2015), Keio University (attested 2015), and Beijing Center for Japanese Studies (2003).

In linguistics, he studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and director of the BAULT research community (~2008–2013).
